headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to reduce residential electricity costs by shifting certain grid infrastructure and capacity costs onto large energy users, primarily data centers.
status: Last Action: Approved by Governor-Chapter 1123 (effective 7/1/2026) on 2026-05-14
supporters: State Senator Louise Lucas, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Dominion Energy (initially), Virginia Conservation Network.
opponents: Data Center Coalition, critics of Governor's amendments.
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a measure designed to shift more energy costs onto data centers to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics, including the bill's patrons and Dominion Energy, expressed concerns that the Governor's amendments might weaken the bill's original goals.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water users supplying data centers to report monthly or quarterly water consumption data, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Potomac Conservancy, Friends of the Rappahannock, environmental groups, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: Data centers drinking Potomac River resources, transparency needed.
news_summary: Potomac Conservancy is advocating for SB 553, a bill that mandates data centers to report their water usage to the State Water Control Board. This transparency is crucial for understanding and addressing the increasing water demands of data centers in the Potomac River region, which faces potential water supply issues by 2030.

headline: Local Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires Virginia local governments to review and amend zoning ordinances to designate data centers as industrial uses, consider proximity to residential areas, and implement noise mitigation requirements.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Environmental and conservation groups, neighborhood associations, historic preservation advocates, farmland protection groups, local planning and public health organizations, Del. John Chilton McAuliff.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations, pro-growth business groups.
news_headline: Loudoun County officials discuss data center noise mitigation.
news_summary: Residents in Loudoun County are experiencing significant noise pollution from data centers, leading to complaints and calls for stricter regulations. Local officials are exploring legislative avenues to address the specific type of noise produced by these facilities, highlighting the growing conflict between industry expansion and community quality of life.
